column1: # The mirror of forward.rules.tsv, and the same format: kind <TAB> from <TAB> to. See that file
# for what each rule kind means; nothing here re-explains them.
# Read this first, because the direction is not symmetric in the way it looks.
# NAMING. A NeoForge 1.21.1 mod is compiled against *official* Mojang names. A Forge 1.20.1 mod
# is compiled against *SRG* names, and that is what the 1.20.1 runtime resolves. So the backward
# direction has to remap official -> SRG, which is mappings/srg2official.tsv read the other way
# round. Analysis is done against a vanilla+Forge jar remapped to official names, so both sides
# of every comparison speak the same language; only the emitted bytecode is SRG.
# DIRECTION OF LOSS. Forward, the hard cases are things 1.21 *added* that a 1.20.1 mod cannot
# know about, and the fallback is usually an inert placeholder. Backward, the hard cases are
# things 1.21 added that a 1.20.1 *game* cannot represent at all -- data components, data-driven
# enchantments, the whole 1.21.1-only datapack tree. There is no 1.20.1 shape for some of it, and
# a rule that invents one is worse than a rule that is missing. Expect REMOVED to carry more
# weight here than it does forward.
# Mined from the two platform jars -- neoforge-21.1.248.jar against
# forge-1.20.1-47.4.22-universal.jar -- for the same reason the forward set is: a data/c/tags/
# file in some mod proves only that a mod author invented that name.
# THE DEFAULT IS NOT SYMMETRIC, and this is the single most important fact about translating
# tags backward. Forward, a forge: tag with no rule is swapped to c: and is almost always right,
# because 1.21 kept the names. Backward, of NeoForge's 348 common tag paths only 139 have a
# 1.20.1 counterpart -- 36 more are renames, and 173 do not exist in Forge 1.20.1 at all. So the
# plain swap is wrong about half the time, and TAG_GONE carries most of the weight below rather
# A TAG_GONE tag is still swapped to forge:, so a mod that both defines and uses its own copy
# keeps agreeing with itself. What it loses is agreement with everything else -- and backward
# that is a real loss, because nothing in 1.20.1 populates c:foods/fruit or c:tools/mace.
# No 1.20.1 counterpart. Swapped anyway; nothing else will contribute to them.
# Inverted wholesale from forward.rules.tsv, which is sound here for a reason worth stating:
# that file's TYPE_RENAME set is not a convenience list, it is exactly the set of types the
# *loader* looks up or dispatches by, where a shimmed copy is a different type as far as the
# scan is concerned. That property is symmetric. FML 1.20.1 scans class files for
# `Lnet/minecraftforge/fml/common/Mod;` exactly as FML 1.21.1 scans for its own, and the event
# bus dispatches on the posted object's exact class either way.
# Checked, not assumed, on both counts that can be checked mechanically:
#   * no forward rule shares a target, so the inversion is 1:1 and picks nothing arbitrarily
#   * all 166 inverted targets exist in the Forge 1.20.1 platform (vanilla + universal +
#     eventbus + fmlcore + fmlloader + forgespi + javafmllanguage + distmarker)
# What that does NOT check is whether the target has the members the corpus calls on it, which
# is the failure RenameGaps' warning sections exist for. Run it backward before trusting any of
# INHERITED DEBT, stated rather than discovered later. The forward file marks the LivingHurtEvent
# / LivingDamageEvent / EntityItemPickupEvent renames as load-enabling stopgaps: the event is
# right, the accessors were renamed with it, and a mod that actually receives one takes a
# NoSuchMethodError. Inverting them inherits exactly that trade in the other direction.
# Classified mechanically, not by hand: each candidate was read out of the NeoForge jar and kept
# only if it is an annotation, an enum (which annotations carry as values), or a subclass of
# net/neoforged/bus/api/Event. Everything else -- 128 of the 166 -- went to neoforge-compat,
# because inverting them wholesale first produced 118 rules that resolve to a Forge type without
# the member the corpus calls on it. That is the "rename resolves, mod dies on first call"
# failure RenameGaps warns about, and it is what shim-first exists to avoid.
# NeoForge injects these into a mod's constructor; Forge 1.20.1 calls a no-argument one. 408 of
# the 479 corpus mods declare the injected form, so Translate synthesises the missing ()V and
# fills each parameter from here. Same ARG_FILL table the vanilla passes use -- what can be
# supplied is data, and a parameter with no filler is reported rather than guessed.
# Dist is named post-rename, because it is one of the types the loader scans for inside
# annotations and is therefore renamed to Forge's rather than shimmed.
# Inverted from the forward file: the old and new descriptors swap, and the narrowing hint drops,
# because 1.20.1's parameter is the wider ParticleOptions and needs no cast to reach it.
# 1.21 gave BlockBehaviour a public properties() accessor. 1.20.1 keeps the field protected and
# offers Properties.copy(BlockBehaviour) instead, so the instance call becomes a static one with
# the receiver as its argument -- which is what METHOD_TO_STATIC is for.
# Not an exact equivalence, and the difference is worth knowing: properties() hands back the live
# object, copy() makes a new one. Mods call this to derive a new block's properties from an
# existing block, where copying is the intent anyway; a mod mutating the returned object expecting
# to change the original would not be doing something 1.20.1 supports in any case.
# Both owners, because the call site's owner is whatever the mod's variable was typed as.
# --- Renames justified by an identical surface, not by loader scanning -------------------------
# The forward file allows a rename on two grounds: the loader dispatches by the type, or the whole
# surface is verified identical. This is the second. DeferredSoundType and ForgeSoundType have the
# same superclass, the same five-Supplier constructor and the same five accessors -- checked with
# javap against both platform jars, not assumed from the names.
# The block above was derived by inverting forward.rules.tsv, and that was the wrong source. It
# only ever covered types the *forward* direction happened to need a rule for, which is not the
# same set as the types this direction's corpus references -- GatherDataEvent is a mod-bus event
# named by 163 ATM10 jars and had no forward rule, so it was missing here and every mod using it
# failed on a class that should never have been shimmed in the first place.
# So the classification was re-run over all 548 referenced NeoForge types that RenameGaps could
# suggest a same-named Forge counterpart for, using the same mechanical test: keep it only if it
# is an annotation, an enum, or a subclass of net/neoforged/bus/api/Event. 263 qualify, and all
# 263 targets exist in the Forge 1.20.1 platform.
# The remaining 285 are shim work and stay out of here on purpose -- that is the boundary the
# 118-warning experiment established, and widening it would walk straight back into it.
# 1.21 renamed Properties.copy to ofFullCopy and added a shallower copyOf beside it. Same shape,
# same static, so a plain call-site rewrite. Found by allthecompressed at registration.
# --- Renames justified by a verified-identical surface -----------------------------------------
# The second justification, applied mechanically instead of one launch at a time. For each of the
# 285 candidates the loader-scanning test did *not* claim, both types were read out of their
# platform jars and their public and protected member sets compared -- names and descriptors, with
# the two loaders' package prefixes collapsed so that a method returning IItemHandler matches the
# one returning IItemHandler. 138 are identical; the other 147 genuinely differ and stay shim work.
# IItemHandler is the example that prompted this: six methods, byte-identical on both sides, and it
# was about to be hand-written as a shim because a launch happened to name it. Discovering that one
# type at a time would have taken 138 launches.
# The rejections are as informative as the promotions -- IEventBus differs 13 members to 14, which
# is exactly why it is hand-shimmed above.
